\n= 1 - 2\" id=\"MathJax-Element-60-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">2–√2\n\n, எனில் x3\" id=\"MathJax-Element-61-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">x3x3\n\n+ 1x3\" id=\"MathJax-Element-62-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">1x31x3\n\n-ன் மதிப்பைக் கண்டறியவும்.\n2f:T65b,\n4 - 2 Shortcut Trick\n

If x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k(k2 − 3).

\n

Given k = 1 − √2, we first find k2 = (1 − √2)2 = 3 − 2√2.

\n

Then, k2 − 3 = 3 − 2√2 − 3 = −2√2.

\n

Now multiply by k: (1 − √2) × (−2√2) = −2√2 + 4 = 4 − 2√2.

\n

∴ The correct answer is 4 − 2√2.

\n\n

Alternate Method

\n

Given:

\n

x + 1/x = 1 − √2

\n

Formula Used:

\n

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

\n

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = (x + 1/x)3 − 3(x + 1/x)

\n

Calculations:

\n

⇒ Let x + 1/x = k = 1 − √2

\n

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k = k(k2 − 3)

\n

⇒ Now, squaring both sides of k = 1 − √2

\n

⇒ k2 = 12 + (√2)2 − 2 × 1 × √2

\n

⇒ k2 = 1 + 2 − 2√2 = 3 − 2√2

\n

⇒ Now compute the term (k2 − 3):

\n

⇒ k2 − 3 = (3 − 2√2) − 3 = −2√2

\n

⇒ Substitute the values back into the expression k(k2 − 3):

\n

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = (1 − √2) × (−2√2)

\n

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = (1 × −2√2) − (√2 × −2√2)

\n

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = −2√2 − (−4) = 4 − 2√2

\n

∴ The correct answer is 4 − 2√2.

\n\n

Additional Information

\n

Cube of a Binomial

\n

The formula for the sum of cubes is derived from: (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b). Rearranging this gives a3 + b3 = (a + b)3 − 3ab(a + b).

\n

Algebraic Identities for Squares

\n

If x + 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 − 2. This identity is extremely useful for stepping up to higher even powers directly.

\n

Algebraic Identities for Differences

\n

If x − 1/x = k, then the corresponding difference formulas are x3 − 1/x3 = k3 + 3k, and x2 + 1/x2 = k2 + 2.

\n\n

Calculation:

\n\n

Let the number be 100x

\n\n

According to the question,

\n\n

100x × (80 – 65)% = 135 

\n\n

⇒ 100x × 15% = 135 

\n\n

⇒ 15x = 135

\n\n

⇒ x = 135/15 

\n\n

⇒ x = 9

\n\n

So, the number is 9 × 100

\n\n

⇒ 900

\n\n

Now, 49% of number = (900 × 49%)

\n\n

⇒ 441

\n\n

∴ 49% of the same number is 441.

ಒಂದೇ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ 80% ಮತ್ತು 65% ರ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ = 135

\n\n

ಲೆಕ್ಕಾಚಾರ:

\n\n

ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ 100x ಆಗಿರಲಿ

\n\n

ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯ ಪ್ರಕಾರ,

\n\n

100x x (80 - 65)% = 135

\n\n

⇒ 100x x 15% = 135

\n\n

⇒ 15x = 135

\n\n

⇒ x = 135/15

\n\n

⇒ x = 9

\n\n

ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ, ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ 9 x 100

\n\n

⇒ 900

\n\n

ಈಗ, ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ 49% = (900 x 49%)

\n\n

⇒ 441

\n\n

∴ ಅದೇ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ 49% 441 ಆಗಿದೆ.

Given:

\n\n

The average of the first three numbers out of four numbers is 18 and that of the last three numbers is 20

\n\n

Last number = 25

\n\n

Concept used:

\n\n

Average = Sum of elements/Number of elements

\n\n

Calculation:

\n\n

Total of 1st three numbers = 18 × 3

\n\n

⇒ 54

\n\n

Total of last three numbers = 20 × 3

\n\n

⇒ 60

\n\n

Now,

\n\n

Sum of 2nd and 3rd number = 60 - 25

\n\n

⇒ 35

\n\n

Now,

\n\n

1st number = 54 - 35

\n\n

⇒ 19

\n\n

∴ The first number is 19.

दिया गया है:

\n\n

चार संख्याओं में से पहली तीन संख्याओं का औसत 18 और अंतिम तीन संख्याओं का औसत 20 है।

\n\n

अंतिम संख्या = 25

\n\n

प्रयुक्त अवधारणा:

\n\n

औसत = पदों का योग/पदों की संख्या

\n\n

गणना:

\n\n

पहली तीन संख्याओं का योग = 18 × 3

\n\n

⇒ 54

\n\n

अंतिम तीन संख्याओं का योग = 20 × 3

\n\n

⇒ 60

\n\n

अब,

\n\n

दूसरी और तीसरी संख्या का योग = 60 - 25

\n\n

⇒ 35

\n\n

अब,

\n\n

पहली संख्या = 54 - 35

\n\n

⇒ 19

\n\n

∴ पहली संख्या 19 है।

చివరి సంఖ్య = 25

\n\n

⇒ 19

∴ మొదటి సంఖ్య 19.

ਚਾਰ ਨੰਬਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਤਿੰਨ ਨੰਬਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਔਸਤ 18 ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਆਖਰੀ ਤਿੰਨ ਨੰਬਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਔਸਤ 20 ਹੈ।

ਆਖਰੀ ਨੰਬਰ = 25

ਵਰਤਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਸੰਕਲਪ:

ਔਸਤ = ਤੱਤਾਂ ਦਾ ਜੋੜ/ ਤੱਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੰਖਿਆ

ਗਣਨਾ:

ਪਹਿਲੀ ਤਿੰਨ ਸੰਖਿਆਵਾਂ ਦਾ ਕੁੱਲ = 18 × 3

⇒ 54

ਆਖਰੀ ਤਿੰਨ ਸੰਖਿਆਵਾਂ ਦਾ ਕੁੱਲ = 20 × 3

⇒ 60

ਹੁਣ,

ਦੂਜੇ ਅਤੇ ਤੀਜੇ ਨੰਬਰ ਦਾ ਜੋੜ = 60 - 25

⇒ 35

ਹੁਣ,

ਪਹਿਲੀ ਸੰਖਿਆ = 54 - 35

⇒ 19

∴ ਪਹਿਲਾ ਨੰਬਰ 19 ਹੈ।

\n\n

Ratio of expenditure of A and B = 3 : 4

Formula used:

\n\n

Income – Savings = Expenditure

Let the income of A and B be 5x and 7x respectively.

\n\n

\n\n

Income of A = 5 × 7000

\n\n

⇒ 35000

\n\n

Income of B = 7 × 7000

\n\n

⇒ 49000

\n\n

Sum of there income = 35000 + 49000

\n\n

⇒ 84000

\n\n

∴ The sum of the incomes (in ₹) of A and B is 84000.

{(5x - 5000) / (7x - 9000)} = (3/4)(₹ में) ज्ञात कीजिये।", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "1,100"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "1,150"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "1,000"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "1,250"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "4", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

Given:

\n\n

A shopkeeper sold an item at 20% gain

\n\n

Concept used:

\n\n

Selling price = Cost price × (100 + profit)%

\n\n

Calculation:

\n\n

Let the cost price of the item be 100a

\n\n

So, selling price = 100a + 120%

\n\n

⇒ 120a

\n\n

Now,

\n\n

In the 2nd case selling price is the same

\n\n

So, the selling price of the 2nd case = 120a

\n\n

According to the question,

\n\n

120a = 125% of cost price    [For 2nd selling]

\n\n

⇒ 120a/125 = 1% of the cost price

\n\n

⇒ (120a/125) × 100 = The cost price

\n\n

⇒ 96a = The cost price  [New cost price]

\n\n

Here,

\n\n

100a - 96a = 50

\n\n

⇒ 4a = 50

\n\n

⇒ a = 50/4 = 12.5

\n\n

So, actual cost price = 100 × 12.5

\n\n

⇒ Rs. 1250

\n\n

∴ The cost price of the item (in ₹) is 1250.

\n\n

यहाँ,

\n\n

100a - 96a = 50

\n\n

⇒ 4a = 50

\n\n

\n\n

\n\n

⇒ 1250 रुपये 

\n\n

∴ वस्तु का क्रय मूल्य (₹ में) 1250 है।

Key Points

\n\n
    \n\t
  • The given sentence is in Indirect Speech. we have to change it into Direct Speech.
    • \n\t
  •  The rules to be followed while changing Indirect Speech into Direct Speech:\n\t
      \n\t\t
    • In the given sentence 'asked' will be changed into 'said to'.
      • \n\t\t
    •  Put a comma after reporting verb and put inverted commas before WH family.
      • \n\t\t
    • The pronoun 'he' will be changed into 'you' because second person will be changed according to the object.
      • \n\t\t
    • Change the past perfect tense into simple past tense.
      • \n\t\t
    •  Remove full stop and Insert question mark after the statement.
      • \n\t
    \n\t
    • \n
\n\n

  Eventually, we got the correct sentence - The chef said to his assistant, "Where did you store the spices?"

\n\n

        \n\t
      •  In blank number 4, we need to fill the blank with the most appropriate preposition from the given four options.
        • \n\t
      • Let's explore the usage of the four given options :\n\t
          \n\t\t
        • At:  is used to show a state, condition, or continuous activity. It is also used to refer to time or place, say where something/somebody is or where something happens..\n\t\t
            \n\t\t\t
          • Example: I was up at 6 am this morning.

          \n\t\t

            \n\t\t\t
          • Example:  I'll explain to you where everything goes.
            • \n\t\t
          \n\t\t
          • \n\t\t
        • ​For: The preposition 'for' is used to show 'purpose or function'. For is used to indicate the period of time, purpose, reason, usage of something.​\n\t\t
            \n\t\t\t
          • Example: Let's decide on the date for the next meet.
            • \n\t\t
          \n\t\t
          • \n\t\t
        • ​On: It is used to indicate a surface, certain side, specify days and dates.\n\t\t
            \n\t\t\t

            • \n\t\t
          \n\t\t
          • \n\t
        \n\t
        • \n\t
      • ​​After understanding the usage of the above proposition, we are sure that the most appropriate preposition is 'for' because it is showing the purpose, reason, and function.
        • \n\t
      • Thus, the correct answer is option 3.
        • \n
      \n\n

      Correct Passage:  I was often invited to colleges and universities to deliver lectures. Once, I went to a university to deliver a lecture.
